binders: A probability measure μ on Ω.
A finite nonnegative real exponent p with 1 ≤ p.
A real-valued function X on Ω.
hypotheses: The measure is a probability measure.
X is almost-everywhere strongly measurable with respect to μ.
conclusions: The Luxemburg gauge generated by ψp(x)=x^(p.toReal) is finite if and only if X belongs to Lp(μ) with exponent ENNReal.ofNNReal p.
mathematical_definitions: The power function ψp is bundled with nonnegativity, convexity, monotonicity, zero value, and divergence at infinity on the nonnegative half-line.
The gauge is the ENNReal infimum of finite positive scales t for which ∫⁻ ofReal(ψp(|X|/t)) dμ ≤ 1.
Gauge membership means the gauge is below ENNReal infinity.
MemLp combines almost-everywhere strong measurability with finite eLpNorm.
translation.proposition_plain_english: On any probability space, for every finite exponent p≥1 and every measurable real random variable X, finite power-Orlicz gauge is equivalent to classical Lp membership.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The exponent is finite and p≥1; p=∞ is excluded.
The theorem is restricted to almost-everywhere strongly measurable real functions.
Admissible scales exclude zero and infinity.
ENNReal.ofReal is harmless on the nonnegative power-function values.
An empty admissible set produces an infinite gauge, so the equivalence is not made vacuous.
